pharm: Water-soluble ionic iodinated contrast agent (diatrizoate salts) that is radiopaque due to its organically bound iodine, providing radiographic opacification of body cavities and the vascular/urinary system.
quick: Retrograde cystourethrography (Cystografin): 25-300 mL instilled to fill the bladder
Bowel prep advised (laxative night before, low-residue diet); not a systemic oral drug
Use only if clearly needed; reproduction studies not conducted
Limited data; iodinated contrast minimally excreted in milk
Risk of contrast-induced nephropathy with intravascular/intravasated use
Observe for hypersensitivity/anaphylactoid reaction; renal function; thyroid function
summary: Diatrizoic acid (diatrizoate, e.g., diatrizoate meglumine - Cystografin) is an FDA-approved ionic iodinated radiographic contrast medium. Cystografin is indicated for retrograde cystourethrography, instilled into the bladder via sterile catheter. Like other iodinated contrast media, it can cause hypersensitivity or anaphylactoid reactions (more likely with asthma, significant allergies, or prior contrast reactions), and intravasation may produce systemic reactions. Iodinated contrast can also cause contrast-induced nephropathy and uncommonly thyroid dysfunction.
indications: Retrograde cystourethrography (bladder/urethra opacification via Cystografin formulation)
Diatrizoate salts are more broadly used as iodinated radiographic contrast for genitourinary, gastrointestinal, and other radiographic/excretory studies depending on the specific formulation

dosage.d: 25-300 mL (amounts >300 mL if bladder capacity allows)
dosage.n: Dose varies with patient age and bladder irritability

dosage.d: Dilute with sterile water or saline (e.g., 30% down to ~18% w/v diatrizoate meglumine)
dosage.n: e.g., 100 mL bottle + 50 mL diluent gives 20% w/v / 9.4% bound iodine

dosage.d: 300 mg/mL diatrizoate meglumine (~141 mg organically bound iodine/mL) for the 30% solution

admin: Appropriate bowel preparation is desirable (laxative the night before, low-residue diet the day before)
Use sterile technique; instill via a sterile catheter and suitable sterile administration set after sterile catheterization
Fill the bladder to capacity for best results; avoid excessive pressure, rapid or acute distention, and trauma
Bladder discomfort, reflux, or spontaneous voiding usually indicates the bladder is full
Take a scout film before contrast and use standard radiographic technique
Have emergency resuscitation equipment and drugs immediately available
moa: Diatrizoate contains organically bound iodine that attenuates X-rays, rendering the structures it fills (e.g., the bladder and urethra) radiopaque for radiographic imaging. It is not pharmacologically active.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to salts of diatrizoic acid
relative: Personal or family history of bronchial asthma, significant allergies, or previous reactions to contrast agents (extreme caution)
Sensitivity to iodine or other contrast agents (not absolute, but use extreme caution)
Known active infectious process of the urinary tract (perform retrograde study with caution)
monitor: Hypersensitivity/anaphylactoid reactions during and after administration

preg: Animal reproduction studies have not been conducted with diatrizoate meglumine. It is not known whether it can cause fetal harm or affect reproductive capacity; administer to a pregnant woman only if clearly needed.
lact: Specific data for this formulation are limited; iodinated contrast media are generally minimally excreted in breast milk and poorly absorbed by the infant.
renal: Retrograde instillation is largely local; however, intravasation or intravascular exposure to iodinated contrast carries a risk of contrast-induced nephropathy - use caution in renal impairment.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is described in labeling.

moderate: Metformin - iodinated contrast that reaches the circulation can increase risk of lactic acidosis with renal impairment (general iodinated-contrast precaution)
interactions.food: Bowel preparation recommended before the procedure
interactions.diagnostics: Contrast agents may interfere with some urine chemical determinations - collect urine before administration or two or more days afterward; iodinated contrast can interfere with thyroid function tests and radioiodine uptake

serious: Perforation of the urethra or bladder
Introduction of infection into the genitourinary tract
Thyroid suppression / hypothyroidism (uncommon, including in infants)
rare: Systemic reactions if intravasation occurs (as with IV contrast)
emergency: Severe anaphylactoid reaction: facial/glottic edema, respiratory distress, convulsions, or shock - may be fatal unless promptly controlled

monitoring: Continuous observation for hypersensitivity/anaphylactoid reactions during and after the procedure
Readiness for emergencies: clear airway, oxygen, and resuscitative drugs immediately available
Renal function if intravasation or intravascular exposure occurs
Thyroid function tests, particularly in infants/neonates, given the risk of transient thyroid suppression
Signs of urinary tract injury or infection after the procedure
counsel: This is an imaging dye placed into the bladder through a catheter for an X-ray study, not a regular medicine
Tell the team about any allergy to iodine, contrast dye, asthma, or prior contrast reactions
Report difficulty breathing, swelling, rash, or feeling faint immediately during or after the test
Some bladder discomfort, urge to urinate, or a small amount of blood in the urine can occur afterward
Follow the bowel-prep instructions (laxative and low-residue diet) before the exam
pk: Not applicable for retrograde instillation (locally cleared on voiding)
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from strong light; use diluted solutions immediately
pearls: Diatrizoate IS an FDA-approved iodinated radiographic contrast medium (e.g., Cystografin = diatrizoate meglumine)
A history of iodine or contrast sensitivity is not an absolute contraindication but demands extreme caution and emergency readiness
Anaphylactoid reactions are more likely with asthma, significant allergies, or prior contrast reactions
If intravasation occurs, expect possible systemic (IV-type) contrast reactions
Iodinated contrast can transiently suppress thyroid function - relevant especially in neonates and infants
Collect urine samples before contrast or 2+ days after, since contrast can interfere with urine chemistry
missed: Not applicable - this is a single-administration diagnostic contrast agent used during an imaging procedure, not a scheduled maintenance medication.
overdose: Excessive bladder filling or pressure can cause discomfort, reflux, or trauma/perforation. Manage by drainage and supportive care; treat any hypersensitivity reaction with standard emergency measures (airway, oxygen, epinephrine, resuscitative drugs).
